rationale:
The initial generator chooses a distant goal without checking push access or connectivity around the crate. This plausibly explains valid but unsolvable outputs; the evidence does not establish a single failure mechanism.

This replacement constructs a two-pull feasibility certificate, then extends one bounded reverse trajectory. Every pull checks both support cells and agent connectivity with the crate occupied. Reversing the trajectory provides legal pushes to the goal. Endpoint selection preserves Manhattan distance >= 2, and agent relocation preserves access to the first push. Ordered sample coordinates control deterministic variation in placement, turns, trajectory length and approach distance.

Obstacles remain exactly sample[:-3]. Static component caches use quadratic space in at most 64 free cells; construction is bounded and performs no joint-state search or whole-scene rejection. If no two-pull certificate exists, the fallback preserves validity without claiming solvability. No candidate code was executed, and no improvement rate is claimed.
